 Order
1. Delay condoned.
2. Leave granted.
3. We have perused the consent terms dated 06.01.2024.
There is no dispute that the consent terms have been signed by the appellant-wife and the first respondent-husband as well as by their respective Advocates.
4. The appellant-wife is present in the Court.
5. The marriage between the parties was solemnized on 12.12.2009.
They have been residing separately from the year 2011.
After realising that the differences between them cannot be ironed out, by consent, they have agreed to dissolve their marriage as per the provisions of Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

6. Considering the fact that the parties are residing separately for more than 12 years, we are of the view that this is a fit case to exercise our jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India for dissolving their marriage.

7. Clauses 1 to 14 of the consent terms read thus: -

(1) Both the parties will file joint application to convert the Divorce proceeding into mutual petition U/s. 13B being Marriage Petition no. 50 of 2012 renumbered at M.P.

The Party of the First part agrees to remain present before the Honble Family Court at Belapur on prior intimation and the party of the Second part undertakes to withdraw the appeal being PWDV Appeal No. 18/2019 (New No. 29/2023).

(2) That the party of the First part has agreed to settle her entire matrimonial claims,
alimony, temporary and permanent and claim against house etc. full and finally at Rs. 46,00,000/- payable by party of the Second part as under.

The party of the First part hereby agrees and undertakes to accept the aforesaid full and final settlement amount, as full and final settlement inclusive of alimony, temporary and permanent maintenance, arrears, including that of purchase of house and all other claims of whatsoever nature against party of Second part.

The party of the Second part will agrees to pay the said amount in following manner: -
i) Rs. 35,00,000/- (Rupees Thirty Five Lakhs Only) will be paid at the time of conversion of the said Petition into 13B petition pending before the Family court Belapur.
ii) Rs. 11,00,000/- (Rupees Eleven Lakhs Only) will be paid when the party of the First part appears and gives consent in Cri. Writ Petition/Cri Application proceeding for quashing by consent of 498A proceedings before the Honble high court filed by the party of the Second part.

(3) Upon receipt of the amount of Rs. 35,00,000/-
(Rupees Thirty Five Lakhs Only) by the First party

, the first party undertakes to withdraw the complaint filed under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 being M.A. no.

sentences.text: (5) Both the parties will have no claims of whatsoever nature against each other.

(6) Both the parties have permanently and irrevocably waived their respective rights, if any, in moveable and immovable property against each other, hence it is also agreed between both the above-named parties that there is no matrimonial property possessed and/or owned by the party of the first part and the party of the Second part.
(7) It is agreed that both the above-named parties will cooperate with each other to ensure proper compliance of the Consent Terms.
(8) Both the parties agree and undertake not to withdraw their consent after the signing of the consent terms.

(9) Both the parties agree not to pursue or press for police complaints, if any, filed by them or any other proceedings pending against each other and the same shall be withdrawn by either party if filed.
(10) It is agreed between both the parties they will not interfere in each others Personal life in any manner in future.

(11) It is agreed between both the parties that this consent terms shall be binding upon the parties,
their successors, heirs, assigns and representatives.
(12) Both the parties hereby withdraw all the allegations made against each other in the present proceedings.
(13) Both the parties have arrived at these consent terms at their own free will, without any force or coercion from anyone.
Both the parties have read over and fully understood the content of these consent terms and have given their respective statements.
(14) Both the parties hereby undertake and agree to abide by the terms of present Consent Terms.

6. In terms of the clause 2 of the consent terms, the three demand drafts dated 30.01.2024 in the sums of Rs. 35,00,000/- bearing no. 000492, Rs. 6,00,000/- bearing no. 032285 and Rs.
5,00,000/- bearing no. 032286 have been handed over by the learned counsel appearing for the first respondent-husband to the learned counsel appearing for the appellant-wife, who in turn has handed over the three demand drafts to the appellant-wife, who is present in the Court.

7. In exercise of powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, we dissolve the marriage solemnized on 12.12.2009 between the appellant-wife, Mrs. Dhanshree Devendra Thakur @ Sapana Ghanshyam Patil and the first respondent-husband, Mr. Devendra Parshuram Thakur by a decree of divorce under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
